newsitem.title: UK: Blair promises "substantial" devolution to Scots.
newsitem.headline: Blair promises "substantial" devolution to Scots.

text.p: Thursday's White Paper on government proposals for a Scottish parliament will offer "a substantial measure of devolution" to people north of the border, Prime Minister Tony Blair said on Monday.
Interviewed on BBC radio, Blair said the proposals would give the new parliament the power to run its own education and health systems and administer the existing separate Scottish legal system.
"This is a substantial measure of devolution. It means that the Scots will be able to take decisions over their legal system...their schools, their hospitals in the way that they want," Blair said.
Blair, who himself grew up in Scotland, said he found "no desire whatever" in the country for Scotland to leave the United Kingdom".
"What everyone is looking for is a way of decentralising government, giving the Scots the recognition that they are a separate nation within the United Kingdom but staying inside the UK," he said.
The government will publish proposals for a Welsh senate on Tuesday. Both sets of proposals will be subject to referenda in the two countries in September.

Blair stressed it would be up to the Welsh people to decide whether to accept plans for the new body in Cardiff. "We don't want them to say no', of course, but it is a decision for the people of Wales," he said.
He added: "If I was in Wales I would be voting yes' because I think it is good to have a strong Welsh voice. It is good for Welsh business and jobs and inward investment and for the local services."
